items.stem: Before building a custom classifier, a team wants a quick quality reference with minimal effort. What is the sensible first step on Vertex AI?

options.text: Establish a baseline using a foundation model
options.rationale: Correct: a foundation-model baseline is fast and sets a reference to beat.

options.text: Train a large custom model immediately
options.rationale: Custom training is costly before a baseline exists.
Deploying first skips the quality check.

options.text: Delete the labelled data to save storage
options.rationale: Labelled data is needed for evaluation and tuning.

items.explanation: Correct: a foundation-model baseline is fast and sets a reference to beat.

items.stem: Which TWO practices support honest model evaluation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Measure quality on a held-out test set the model did not train on
options.rationale: Correct: held-out data gives an unbiased estimate.

options.text: Report the metric relevant to the task, not just overall accuracy
options.rationale: Correct: task-appropriate metrics avoid misleading conclusions.

options.text: Evaluate only on the training data
Pick the metric after seeing which one looks best
options.rationale: Choosing metrics post hoc biases the result.

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

items.stem: A deployed Vertex AI endpoint serves few requests but keeps incurring cost. What is the most likely cause to check first?

options.text: The endpoint keeps provisioned resources running while idle
options.rationale: Correct: endpoints can hold resources and bill even when idle.
A closed notebook does not drive endpoint cost.

options.text: The training data is too small
options.rationale: Dataset size is unrelated to idle serving cost.
Accuracy does not cause idle cost.

items.explanation: Correct: endpoints can hold resources and bill even when idle.
